doc_description: Operations and maintenance agreement between Westmere Industrial Park Authority and Sunhaven Energy Operations Ltd. for a 7.5 MWdc solar array and 4 MW/16 MWh battery microgrid in the fictional North Basin Industrial Park, Nevada, covering service terms, performance guarantees, fees, incident response, safety, insurance and dispute resolution.

structure.title: Page 001 - Parties, Purpose and Contract Structure
structure.summary: This operations and maintenance agreement between Westmere Industrial Park Authority (Owner) and Sunhaven Energy Operations Ltd. (Operator), effective 10 March 2027, covers a distributed generation system in the fictional North Basin Industrial Park, Nevada. Operator provides preventive and corrective maintenance, remote monitoring and performance reporting, but may not act as electricity retailer and must follow the Owner's dispatch protocol. Covered assets are a 7.5 MWdc solar array, a 4 MW/16 MWh lithium iron phosphate battery, six medium-voltage transformers and a supervisory control system across two yards. Exclusions include the utility feeder, tenant circuits and third-party telecoms, though incident coordination may apply. Operator must reconcile asset records within 30 days, escalating discrepancies above 2 percent. The term runs 1 May 2027 to 30 April 2032, with one optional two-year extension. Mobilization within 20 Business Days covers induction, spares inspection and monitoring handover, and a joint handover report does not waive pre-existing defects. Fees are USD 42,000 monthly, parts over USD 2,500 need written approval unless safety requires immediate replacement, and emergency call-outs cost USD 145 per technician-hour. Invoicing is monthly in arrears, payable within 25 days, with late interest of 0.75 percent per month.

structure.title: Page 005 - Preventive Maintenance and Response Times
structure.summary: The document sets out operator obligations for a microgrid service contract. Preventive maintenance includes monthly inverter inspections, quarterly infrared thermography, annual protective relay tests and six-monthly battery fire-suppression checks, all recorded against asset identifiers. Critical incidents need remote acknowledgement within 10 minutes and on-site attendance within two hours; high incidents affecting over 20 percent of capacity need acknowledgement within 30 minutes. Maintenance may be deferred only for weather, permit or safety reasons, with an Owner-approved record. The PV availability guarantee is 98.5 percent, with a fee reduction of 1 percent per 0.5-point shortfall, capped at 6 percent and serving as the sole price remedy. Battery throughput is not guaranteed because Owner controls dispatch. Safety requires permits, lockout-tagout, arc-flash controls, a emergency plan and two drills yearly. Battery waste must be handled as regulated, and electrolyte releases reported within one hour. Monthly reports are due by the fifth Business Day, with telemetry kept 24 months. Critical spares, subcontracting with Owner approval, cybersecurity controls with two-hour breach notice, and insurance limits (USD 3 million general liability, USD 2 million professional liability) are also covered.

structure.title: Page 009 - Insurance, Liability and Termination
structure.summary: This operation and maintenance agreement for a solar-plus-battery microgrid sets service, safety, reporting and legal terms. Operator must inspect inverter stations monthly, run thermography quarterly, test protective relays annually and check battery fire-suppression controls every six months, logging all work against asset IDs. Critical incidents require remote acknowledgement within 10 minutes and on-site attendance within two hours; High incidents affecting over 20% of capacity need acknowledgement within 30 minutes. Deferrals are allowed only for weather, permit or safety reasons, with Owner approval. Operator guarantees 98.5% annual PV availability, with a fee reduction of 1% per 0.5-point shortfall, capped at 6% and serving as the sole remedy. The battery throughput is not guaranteed. Safety duties include permits, lockout-tagout, arc-flash controls, two drills a year and damaged-battery handling, with electrolyte releases reported within one hour. Monthly reports are due by the fifth Business Day, and telemetry is kept for 24 months. Spares, approved subcontracting, cybersecurity (MFA, breach notice within two hours) and insurance limits are specified. Liability is capped at 12 months of fees, and termination is permitted after three critical response failures in a rolling year. Exit support runs for 45 days, billed at USD 95 per hour above 40 hours. Formal notices must go by courier or registered mail. Nevada law governs, and mediation in Reno for 20 Business Days precedes litigation.

structure.title: Page 010 - Exit Assistance, Notices and Disputes
structure.summary: The text covers liability, default, exit, notices and disputes. Operator's aggregate contractual liability is capped at 100 percent of the fixed service fees paid or payable in the preceding twelve months, except for fraud, intentional wrongdoing and bodily injury caused by negligence. A material nonmonetary breach may be cured within 30 calendar days after written notice. Termination is permitted after an opportunity to respond in writing if Critical Incident response fails on three separate occasions within any rolling twelve months. In the final 45 days of the term, Operator must provide a live defect register, updated asset inventory, inspection history and operating credentials to Owner's replacement operator. Exit support beyond 40 labor-hours is billed at USD 95 per hour with prior written approval. Formal notices must go by courier or registered mail to the signature-page addresses, with an optional email copy; a message sent only to the operations helpdesk is not formal notice. Nevada law governs. Before an ordinary contractual lawsuit, senior representatives must attempt good-faith mediation in Reno, Nevada, for at least 20 Business Days after a written mediation request.
